a: Put these steps in correct order for a retry-with-error-feedback extraction flow
items: Run the extraction via tool_use against the JSON schema
Validate the structured output (e.g., Pydantic or JSON schema checks)
Detect a semantic failure, such as line items not summing to the stated total
Send a follow-up including the original document, the failed extraction, and the specific validation errors
Accept the corrected output, or route to human review if the information is absent from the source
b: Extract → validate → detect semantic failure → retry with specific error feedback → accept or route to review
notes: Appending the specific validation error guides self-correction for format/structural failures; recognizing absent-information cases prevents wasted retries.

a: Your support resolution agent (MCP tools: get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human) has a system prompt requiring identity verification before refunds and capping autonomous refunds at $500. Production logs show 3% of refunds processed without a verified customer ID, and last week it refunded $1,200 in one turn. When it does escalate, human agents receive no case context and restart from scratch. Design the fix — what do you change and why?
b: Replace prompt-based enforcement with programmatic controls: a prerequisite gate that blocks process_refund (and lookup_order where needed) until get_customer returns a verified customer ID, plus a tool-call interception hook that blocks refunds over $500 and redirects to escalate_to_human. Keep prompt guidance for tone, but treat it as probabilistic. On escalation, compile a structured handoff summary (customer ID, root cause, refund amount, recommended action) since humans lack the transcript.
rubric: Identifies that prompt instructions have a non-zero failure rate and replaces them with programmatic enforcement (prerequisite gate blocking process_refund until get_customer verifies identity)
Adds a tool-call interception hook that deterministically blocks refunds above $500 and redirects to the human-escalation workflow
Specifies a structured handoff protocol (customer ID, root cause, amount, recommended action) so human agents without transcript access can act
notes: Deterministic compliance for financial operations requires hooks and gates; the handoff summary requirement comes from Task 1.4's mid-process escalation protocol.

a: Your CI pipeline invokes Claude Code on every push to a PR for automated review. Developers complain the bot re-posts the same findings after each new commit, its output format varies so your comment-posting script frequently fails to parse it, and its generated test suggestions duplicate scenarios the existing test suite already covers. Design the fix — what do you change and why?
b: Run Claude Code with -p plus --output-format json and --json-schema so findings are machine-parseable for inline comment posting. On re-runs, include the prior review findings in context and instruct Claude to report only new or still-unaddressed issues. For test generation, provide the existing test files in context so duplicates are avoided, and document testing standards and available fixtures in CLAUDE.md to raise suggestion quality.
rubric: Uses --output-format json with --json-schema (alongside -p) to enforce machine-parseable structured findings instead of free-form text
Includes prior review findings in context on re-runs with an instruction to report only new or unaddressed issues, eliminating duplicate comments
Provides existing test files in context and documents testing standards/fixtures in CLAUDE.md so test generation avoids already-covered scenarios
notes: All three fixes come from Task 3.6: structured CLI output for automation, prior-findings context for deduplication, and CLAUDE.md as the CI context mechanism.

concept: Architect·F — Extraction Schema and Validation Design
a: Your invoice-extraction pipeline uses tool_use with a strict JSON schema where every field is required. QA finds that when a PO number is absent from a document the model invents a plausible one, that extracted line items sometimes don't sum to the stated total yet pass validation, and that your retry loop burns three attempts on documents where the missing data simply doesn't exist. Design the fix — what do you change and why?
b: Make fields that may be absent optional/nullable so the model can return null instead of fabricating values. Add semantic self-checks the schema alone can't provide: extract calculated_total alongside stated_total and flag discrepancies with a conflict_detected boolean. Restrict retry-with-error-feedback to format and structural errors, and short-circuit to human review when validation indicates the information is absent from the source, since retries cannot recover missing data.
rubric: Changes required fields to optional/nullable so absence is representable and fabrication pressure is removed
Adds semantic validation beyond schema syntax — e.g., calculated_total vs stated_total comparison with a conflict/discrepancy flag
Distinguishes retryable format or structural errors from absent-information cases, stopping retries and routing the latter to human review
notes: Strict schemas eliminate syntax errors only; nullable fields prevent fabrication, semantic cross-checks catch wrong-but-well-formed output, and retry limits come from Task 4.4.
